Approves a Salary Increase for Legislative Secretary Resolution #10 Councilman Beyrodt: “Approves a Salary Increase for Legislative Secretary, so moved.” Councilman Rothwell: “Seconded.” Supervisor Aguiar: “Vote please.” The Vote: “Kern, yes; Rothwell, yes; Beyrodt.” Councilman Beyrodt : “Thank you to Ca rol. She does a great job and it’s well deserved, yes.” Vote Continued: “Hubbard, yes; Aguiar.” Supervisor Aguiar : “Bill, I have a question. This raise, does that include the five percent we gave the town, every employee? Where’s Bill? Every employee got a five percent raise. I want to know if this is an additional raise because this did not go through the process. This did not go through the budgetary process, myself, Bill. Yeah go ahead.” Bill Rothaar : “This is just a straight seven and a half percent increase over the 2022 salary filing.” Supervisor Aguiar: “Right, so it’s not, she doesn’t get an additional five percent?” Bill Rothaar: ‘She did not get the step we spoke about earlier.” Supervisor Aguiar : “Okay so seventy -five. I’m going to vote no. This did not go through the process. You weren’t aware of it. The labor attorney wasn’t aware of it, myself as the budget officer, so I’m going to vote no.” Julie O’Neill: “Resolution is adopted.”

Approves Salary Increase for Assistant Town Engineer Resolution #20 Councilman Kern: “Approves Salary Increase for Assistant Town Engineer, so moved.” Councilman Hubbard: “Seconded.” Supervisor Aguiar: “Vote please.” The Vote: “Kern, yes; Rothwell, yes; Beyrodt.” Councilman Beyrodt: “I’d like to take a moment to echo the words of Mike who spoke eloquently about the great work that happens with our town employees every single day. I got a text message from Ken Testa this morning saying that the fire negotiated increase was not reflected in this resolution and he was promised something other than what this resolution says. Unless Bill can come up and say otherwise, I’d like to vote no on this, but I’d like to hear your input before and I only bring it up as liaison to the engineering department and we have a great engineering department led by Drew Dillingham. They do great work and by the way we’re about to incumber on the town square which the engineering department is intimately working with and the conversion of Second Street which they are intimately working on it. So, I just want to make sure that what he was promised is in this resolution.” Bill Rothaar : “So this resoluti on does not get him to the twelve thousand, the potential increase in the CSCA contract which he will benefit from would get him to that twelve thousand that he was told.” Councilman Beyrodt : “And during budget negotiations that was explained to him?” Bill Rothaar : “No, budget negotiations, that wasn’t explained to him. He wasn’t in on the budget negotiations but there was a conversation after that where he asked about it and we explained to him that with the three, with the step with the five percent and with the union increase he’s also entitled to, he will get to that twelve thousand.” Councilman Beyrodt: “Understood. I vote no, thank you.” Vote Continued: “Hubbard, yes; Aguiar.” Supervisor Aguiar: Yes, it’s built in and I researched it last night. We have to wait for the contract. He wanted close to twelve thousand dollars. I think it comes up to eleven thousand eight hundred which is pretty substantial raise. I think it’s actually the highest or one of the highest received so it is built into it. We just have to settle our contract negotiations and he misunderstood. He did text everybody. Bill did explain it to him yesterday. I think he’s going to be reaching eleven thousand eight hundred so I’m going to vote yes.” Councilman Rothwell : “(Inaudible ) KEN Testa is just absolutely incredible. He’s one of the town’s top employees and Frank and I’m absolutely looking out to make sure that he’s protected. I did have a meeting with him, and Councilman Hubbard was on the cell phone when we discussed this an d when we calculated everything right now we are still in negotiations with the union contract but should it fall in the market of five thousand he’ll be receiving twelve thousand two hundred and fifty-eight dollars so he gets his raise and that’s part of the conversation we had with him so he will receive what was promised.” Julie O’Neill: “Resolution was adopted.”

Appoints Financial Advisor Resolution #32 Councilman Kern: “Appoints Financial Advisor, so moved.” Councilman Hubbard: “Seconded.” Supervisor Aguiar: “Vote please.” The Vote: “Kern, yes; Rothwell, yes; Beyrodt, yes; Hubbard, yes Aguiar.” Supervisor Aguiar : “Bill, can you ju st give me a little bit of a background. Is Bill here, on this resolution please? Who is this person and what are they charging us? What is their purpose? I know there was a prior resolution right on this.” Bill Rothaar : “So we put out a RFP last year for a financial advisor. Our financial advisor was one who goes out and sells our bonds, files our SEC reports and offering statements in order to sell bonds. So, we went out and did a RFP last year in August or September appointed them and this is just a rea ppointment for the year. Every year we do this for a financial advisor.” Supervisor Aguiar: “Okay.” Vote Continued: “Aguiar, yes. Resolution is adopted.”

Adopts Workplace Violence Protection Program Resolution #36 Councilman Kern: “Adopts Workplace Violence Protection Program, so moved.” Councilman Hubbard: “Seconded.” Supervisor Aguiar: “Vote please.” The Vote: “Kern, yes; Rothwell, yes; Beyrodt, yes; Hubbard, yes; Aguiar.” Supervisor Aguiar: “Yes, and I see that we have this plan in place. Erik, so we’re, can you, now that we’re dealing and catching up with the required federal law saying that we need a workplace violence, we also need the sexual harassment part in place. I think we have that, right that the employees get and we also need to possibly adopt a code of ethics yes.” Erik Howard: “We have that (Inaudible).” Supervisor Aguiar: “Under Article 18 of the general municipal law updating, that’s what all the towns, they update this state contr oller code of ethics and I think we’re the only ones in the town lagging behind and I think we have the OSHEA.” Erik Howard: “(Inaudible).” Supervisor Aguiar: “All the towns won’t be adopting it. Our plan, I actually looked at it today, our ethics code, let me finish. I actually looked at it today before I came here and it’s old. The last amendment was 2004. So, I actually called, I called Southold right before the meeting. I called a bunch of, they’re all adopted, the controller’s, the state controller’s model, so maybe you have to just look at it and update it. I’m going to vote yes but we have to update our codes and our other plans, yes. Resolution is adopted.”

Schedules a Public Hearing and Authorizes Town Clerk to Publish and Post a Public Notice of Public Hearing to Consider a Local Law Imposing a Six (6) Month Moratorium on the Development of Properties Located Within the Industrial A, Industrial B, and Industrial C Zoning Use Districts Within the Hamlet of Calverton (Zip Code 11933) Within the Town of Riverhead Resolution #39 Councilman Hubbard: “Schedules a Public Hearing and Authorizes Tow n Clerk to Publish and Post a Public Notice of Public Hearing to Consider a Local Law Imposing a Six (6) Month Moratorium on the Development of Properties Located Within the Industrial A, Industrial B and Industrial C Zoning Use Districts Within the Hamlet of Calverton (Zip Code 11933) Within the Town of Riverhead so moved.” Councilman Beyrodt: “Second.” Supervisor Aguiar: “Vote please.” The Vote: “Kern.” Councilman Kern : “I going to vote no on this, and I want to be clear from the beginning that I will look at a code with exceptions. I will not do a blanket even for six months moratorium:” Vote Continued: “Rothwell.” Councilman Rothwell : “I think a lot of the problem with development is smore involved with the variances that are given and not necessarily staying within the standards of the current code in place. I just don’t feel like it’s proper for us to take the property rights of owners away by imposing a moratorium. I think the town does need to bring in high-tech jobs and I think it will pl ay outside of the EPCAL facility and the fenced property and the surrounding areas of Calverton, it is the industrial area. I just think voting on a six month moratorium is just a setup for asking developers to pause and to not come to the town and to put off any investments here. Nothing is going to be completed in six months, this we know. I don’t feel anything is going to be completed in a year. If you’re standing by the comprehensive plan, I think eighteen months is a minimum, so I don’t understand and I don’t want to send the wrong message. I know I have absolutely stood up here and I’ve actually said that I’m always open to the public’s input, but I also think that at the same point we have to do our due diligence and I think we’re going to put ourselv es in a very poor legal position as well by stopping moratoriums. We have to, we do listen to the Suffolk County Planning Commission and other aspects of law that is in fact in place and so I know there’s passion behind it and that is a great reason why pe ople would like to see a moratorium. I do like hearing, and I always ask for the publics input but I think this time doing my due diligence and doing my own research I don’t think it’s the right way to proceed and therefore I vote no.” Vote Continued: “Beyrodt.” Councilman Beyrodt : “I would like a little clarification from the town attorney that we’re voting on scheduling a public hearing on a potential six month moratorium only.” Erik Howard: “Yes, that is correct.” Councilman Beyrodt: “I vote yes to give the public hearings.” Vote Continued: “Hubbard.” Councilman Hubbard: “I somewhat offered this. I strongly believe that six months is not long enough, but it was a starting point. I believe we are paying in excess of eight hundred thousand dollars for a comp plan between what we’ve already paid out with one contract and what we’re going to pay out with a future contract. To me you’re just wasting your money if you don’t listen to the comprehensive plan. The last plan was done in 2003. Times have change d drastically since then. Why we need the new comprehensive plan, the new comprehensive plan, nobody is hiding behind it. It will be a way to guide us to proper planning for the Town of Riverhead. Our own Planning Board has recommended this to us. The fact that we don’t want to go at least six months to wait for the comprehensive plan to take a look at the Calverton area first and foremost in regards to Industrial A, B and C, I think that’s a shame that the Board doesn’t want to wait at least six months. Th e developers are sitting out here with bated breath. Six months is not going to hurt them. They’re not going away. Some of these projects even with the comprehensive plan will be coming into town people. I will tell you that. There are going to be certain projects that are going to be coming into town. We are going to have anaerobic digesters in some point in time. We are going to have battery energy storage systems. I’m not against either one of those. What I’m against particularly with this resolution is the massive amounts of development that have come in all at once to one particular area of our town. That’s why the moratorium is needed to pump the brakes, take a look at this, let the experts take a look at it and let us come up with a cohesive comprehen sive plan that will satisfy both the developers and the residents of this town. I absolutely and strongly vote yes to this publish and post.” Vote Continued: “Aguiar.” Supervisor Aguiar : “Well, I’m always open to hearing from the public and I hope that I continue hearing from the public. These projects should never injure our residents, our villages and I am fully supportive of what’s going on but we need the Planning Board and it is their responsibility, that’s why it’s called planning board, and they sh ould be guided by their own commission memos. Again, they punted it to us. One particular person punted it to us and they took a vote on it. I will be sending them their planning commission memo where one member of the planning board is on there. This is n ot researched. This is a faulty resolution. I’ve looked at other resolutions from other towns and there are significant differences. You also have to always put exceptions on it, hardships, that’s not even included here and so given that, I’m not going to vote to hear from the public on a faulty resolution. This should be dealt with and can be dealt with right now through code. That’s what eventually is going to happen. We have a comprehensive plan. They’re telling us fourteen months, that’s going to turn i nto eighteen months, that’s going to turn into two years. After that what’s going to happen we have to do the same thing we could have done today, go to code, change the code and then adopt it, have public hearings and then adopt it. Nothing changes. All w e’re doing is stopping progress here, letting the people know and not handling the problem ourselves. I’m handling the problem. I’m not Densieski who decided to throw it back to us without consulting with us and us working on this. It could be changed righ t now through code. It’s a faulty resolution. It’s (inaudible) by the Suffolk County Planning Commission, advising memo, volume two, issue one, Spring of 1998 and one of the planning members, Richard Dea from Riverhead Town is on that. Be guided by your ow n memo and let’s work together. Let’s get this done and make sure that our communities are not injured, and I’ll be the first one behind you guys supporting you. We don’t want this. We don’t want an over saturation, but we can’t stop progress and it’s real easy. I brought this before all the towns, all the Supervisors, all ten of us are sitting there and there’s that’s (inaudible). You should deal with it, it’s your code, it’s your planning Board. Every single one was saying, how do you do that in Riverhead . Yes, other towns have moratoriums but it’s very limited and it’s not to wait two years, three years. For example, Southampton did a moratorium because all the hotel rooms were turning into condos. So, they had to put a stop just on some items specific, i t was short and they needed the code and they moved forward. I was talking to Hempstead Supervisor. He said we have one in place because we’re ninety -seven percent built out. That’s when you really need a moratorium, when there’s a danger to us and to our town. In our case I’m going to recommend going back to the Planning Board, work with us, help us change our code, continue doing your job. I’m going to vote no.” Julie O’Neill: “Resolution is not adopted.” Councilman Hubbard : “Just for the record I want to say there is nothing illegal about this resolution.”
